steps.title: Saving with a phone
steps.body: In Kenya, many people pay and save with their phone. They often move small amounts, every day or every week. Small amounts add up. If you save €5 every week, you have €260 after one year.

steps.title: Pay yourself first
steps.body: Many people save what is left at the end of the month. Often nothing is left. With [[pay-yourself-first]], you move a fixed amount to savings on the day your pay arrives. You spend the rest. Then saving does not depend on how the month goes.

steps.prompt: The chart shows how a monthly amount grows over the years. Move the monthly amount. Find an amount that gives at least €3,000 after 5 years.
You save €10 every week. You get no interest. How much do you have after one year?
steps.reveal: €520. A year has 52 weeks, and 52 times €10 is €520.

steps.prompt: True or false: saving is only worth it with large amounts.
steps.explanation: False. Small amounts add up over time. A regular habit matters more than the size of one payment.

steps.prompt: With pay yourself first, when do you move money to savings?
options: On the day your pay arrives
At the end of the month, with what is left
Only when you get a bonus
steps.explanation: You move the money first, on payday. Then you spend what is left. This way you do not forget, and you do not spend the money by accident.

steps.title: Your spending and your savings
steps.body: You spend about **{monthlySpending}** a month. You have **{savingsBalance}** in your savings account. A fixed amount on payday makes your savings grow without a new decision each month.

steps.prompt: Your savings account pays {savingsRate} a year. Move the sliders to see what a monthly amount could grow to.

goal.hint: Move a slider to see the result change.

steps.note: The interest slider starts at your real rate. This is an example, not a forecast.

steps.title: Your decision
steps.body: You spend about **{monthlySpending}** a month. What share of your pay do you want to move to savings on payday? You choose the number.
